meta.purpose: Real figures for giving SLATE's household appliances (dishwasher, washer, dryer, refrigerator, oven/range, microwave, air conditioner, water heater, furnace/boiler) faults, repair visits and repair-or-replace decisions, instead of only ageing out. Markets: US (New York, Los Angeles, New Haven), Canada (Toronto, Vancouver), UK (London), Ireland (Dublin), Mexico (Mexico City).
meta.confirmedMeans: confirmed:true only where the figure was read from the publisher's own page on 2026-10-02 (fetched and read as text). confirmed:false where it came from a search engine's summary of a page that could not be read, or from a secondary report of someone else's study.
meta.taxIncludedMeans: true = the page says tax is included; false = the page says tax is extra; null = the page does not say.
meta.cityLevel: No publisher read here gives city-specific appliance repair prices for New York, Los Angeles, New Haven, Toronto or London. Angi's city URLs 404; Thumbtack's New York, Los Angeles and New Haven appliance-repair pages repeat the same national sentence word for word; HomeStars' Toronto and Vancouver price-guide URLs 404. US, Canada and UK rows are therefore national. Vancouver, Dublin and Mexico City rows are from local firms or local-market aggregators and say so.
meta.definitionsWarning: Reliability figures are not comparable across publishers: CR reports 'a problem by end of year 5' (refrigerators with icemakers), 'broke down in years 2-5' (washers) or 'broken down or stopped working as well' over an unbounded ownership period (dishwashers); Which? reports 'proportion faulty in first 7 years' (6 for dishwashers in one release) and shares 'of all faults', not of all machines. See each row's definition.

rates.unit: share of refrigerators with icemakers that will have a problem by the end of the fifth year of ownership
rates.definition: CR estimate from its three most recent annual member surveys: 85,290 refrigerators with icemakers bought new 2016-2026. 'Problem' includes icemaker and dispenser failures as well as compressor failure and not keeping temperature.
rates.note: Page updated September 22, 2026. CR calls refrigerators 'one of the least reliable products we track'.

rates.unit: share of all new refrigerators purchased since 2016 that have experienced at least one specific problem
rates.definition: Cumulative over ownership to date (not time-bounded); 'specific problem such as an inability to make ice or a broken compressor'.
rates.note: Ownership periods vary from <1 to ~10 years, so this is not an annual rate.

rates.unit: share of all refrigerators estimated to require repairs by the end of the fifth year of ownership
rates.definition: CR estimate, all refrigerator types (not only icemaker models).
rates.note: Seen only in a search-engine summary of CR's own X post; not opened. Consistent with the 30% icemaker figure above.

rates.unit: share of washers that broke down during the second through fifth years of ownership
rates.definition: CR 2025 member survey; 'broke down', years 2-5 only (excludes year 1, typically under warranty).
rates.note: Page updated August 16, 2026. Roughly 3.3% a year over years 2-5 if spread evenly (derived, not published).

rates.unit: estimated brand breakage rate by the fifth year of ownership
rates.definition: CR brand-level estimates: agitator top-loaders 10-18%, HE top-loaders 14-23% (Samsung 23%), front-loaders 14-25%.
rates.note: The page was read (95,510 members, 108,608 washers bought new 2015-2025, updated July 30, 2026) but its brand percentages sit behind CR's member wall; these ranges came from a search-engine summary and may be from an earlier edition.

rates.unit: share of members' dishwashers that have broken down or stopped working as well as they should
rates.definition: CR survey of ~77,000 dishwashers across 27 brands bought 2015-2025; cumulative over ownership to date, not time-bounded. CR's brand ratings predict problems in the first five years.

rates.unit: share of a brand's dishwashers developing faults in the first six years of ownership (best brand vs worst brand)
rates.definition: Which? large-appliance survey, July 2025 (3,815 Which? Connect members + 5,561 public).
rates.note: Article dated 19 Dec 2025; brands are not named in the free text. Per-brand 'proportion faulty' tables are members-only.

rates.unit: share of one very reliable hob brand's products developing faults in the first seven years
rates.definition: Which? July 2025 survey; best brand only.
rates.note: Hob (cooktop), not oven. No worst-brand figure given for hobs.

rates.unit: share of one one-star brand's washer-dryers developing faults within the first seven years
rates.definition: Which? July 2025 survey; worst brand only.
rates.note: Useful as an upper bound for a combined machine.

rates.unit: proportion faulty in first 7 years, by brand
rates.definition: Which? reliability star = proportion faulty (50%) + average time to first fault (25%) + impact on day-to-day use (25%); 5,588 washing machines, July 2025; min sample 40 per brand.
rates.note: Method confirmed; the per-brand percentages and 'average time to first fault' are behind Which?'s paywall (£9.99/month digital). Same structure for fridge freezers (5,132 units), tumble dryers (2,692) and dishwashers (3,845).

rates.unit: share of washing machines that get repaired (vs discarded) when they fail
rates.definition: Profeco survey of 5,831 people in the Mexico City metropolitan area. Same table: refrigerators 56.9%; repair cost averaged 18.0% (washer) and 17.9% (refrigerator) of a new appliance's price.
rates.note: Read from a 2004 newspaper's report of a Profeco study, not from Profeco's own page; the study is about 20 years old. This is a repair-uptake share, not a failure rate.

rules.rule: 50% rule: replace if the repair costs 50% or more of a new appliance (including the installation cost of the new one); also consider replacing at roughly 10 years old.
rules.note: Angi worked example: $300 dishwasher + $175 install = $475 basis. Angi also: a 20-year-old appliance is not worth fixing.

rules.rule: Appliances more than 10 years old, or with repairs costing more than 50% of replacement, typically aren't worth repairing.
rules.note: HomeGuide. Appliance-specific: dishwasher consider replacing at 5-8 years; fridge often worth replacing >10 years; oven >10-20 years; washer >10 years for expensive repairs; ice maker repair cheaper than replacement under 5 years.

rules.rule: Repair a dishwasher if it is under eight years old and the repair is under 50% of a new unit.
Replace a central AC rather than repair if: older than 10 years; uses R-22; needs frequent repairs; repair is at least 50% of a new AC; or repair cost × system age in years exceeds $5,000.
Replace a water heater over 10 years old or when repair exceeds 50% of replacement.
Replacing the furnace is typically best for units needing frequent repairs or more than 20 years old.
rules.note: Most heating repairs $100-$600 vs new furnace $3,500-$7,500+.

rules.rule: CR's washer fix-or-nix meter weighs estimated repair cost, original purchase price and current value by years owned; worked example: $650 washer, 7 years old, 7 loads a week → buy new; $1,000 washer, 3 years old → repair.
rules.note: Depreciation-based rather than a fixed %. Most washer warranties last a year (Speed Queen up to 7).

rules.rule: Washers likely uneconomic to repair after 8 years, when maximum repair cost approaches 50% of a new one; refrigerators still worth repairing at 8-10 years; replace an appliance when repair would exceed ~40% of new in its likely-failure age range.
rules.note: Profeco study (2004) as reported by El Siglo de Durango; not Profeco's own page.

rules.rule: Repair first unless the repair costs more than a new appliance.
rules.note: A Dublin firm's own stated policy, not an industry rule.

worthChecking: Lifespan sources disagree sharply on dishwashers: InterNACHI 9 years vs Angi 10-15. A search summary also attributed 'washer 13.4, dishwasher 15.2, refrigerator 14.3 years' to US DOE efficiency-standard analyses — plausible (DOE technical support documents carry average lifetimes) but not read; worth pulling from DOE's TSDs as the most authoritative US lifespans.
HomeStars' fridge 'compressor $25-$260' is implausibly low for a compressor replacement (HomeGuide: $700-$1,250 US); treat as start-relay/minor work.
Angi's overall average ($180, should-I-repair page) differs from a search summary of another Angi page ($170, $100-$240); the read figure is used.
Checkatrade tables headed 'Cost + VAT' — unclear if VAT is included or extra; HomeGuide/Angi/HomeStars never state tax treatment (US/CA services are usually taxed or untaxed by state/province).
D&G one-off repair £150 and boiler £359, and the '85% first-visit fix' — from search summaries only; D&G pages need a browser to read.
Profeco figures are from a 2004 study reported by a newspaper; useful only as ratios (repair ≈ 18% of new price).
CR washer brand breakage ranges 10-25% by year 5 came from a search summary and may be an older edition than the July 2026 page.
InterNACHI 'boiler 40 years' is a North American cast-iron hydronic boiler; do not apply to UK/IE combi boilers (commonly cited at 10-15 years, not read here).
Mexico City price pages are repair firms' marketing; cronoshare.com.mx is the only one stating 'IVA incluido'.
